text:
maya: Heads-up — bringing up summit13b (int4 canary) on dedicated pool. Seeing intermittent OOMs on long summaries and a small quality dip on our summarization eval set. starting triage.

alejandro: OK. first guess is mem fragmentation + prefetched KV pressure. did you try lowering max_new_tokens for the canary?

maya: Default for these builds was 1024. On a few requests we hit OOM in step write_kv_batch, logs attached below.

riju: paste of the tail of the agent log: 
```
E 2026-03-18T14:12:03Z step=write_kv_batch mem_used=28512MB free=256MB slot_alloc_failed
E 2026-03-18T14:12:03Z oom while allocating 48MB for kv_block
W 2026-03-18T14:12:04Z evict_attempts=2 kv_evicted=0
```

riju: also noting a lot of small allocations on the host side from prefetch.

alejandro: two quick mitigations: 1) reduce canary max_new_tokens to 512 or 384, 2) enable aggressive slot compactor (threshold 0.25) for the canary nodes so fragmentation is reclaimed sooner. both are low-risk and fast to rollback.

sasha: on quality: running a quick eval — int4 vs fp16 for summit13b on summarization dev set. initial numbers show ~2.3% ROUGE-1 drop when quantized with default calibration. not huge but noticeable.

maya: thanks. we'll run a paired eval after mem mitigations. priority is keeping service up.

oliver: also try a temporary policy: if latency < 50ms tail, route >512 token requests to fp16 model variant (fallback). that buys us time for quant tuning.

alejandro: agree. add a route rule: generation.max_new_tokens > 512 -> variant: summit13b-fp16-fallback. Should be cheap to implement via routing rules.

maya: I pushed a quick canary config patch:
```
{"max_new_tokens":512, "batch_size":4, "adaptive_batching":{"max_tokens":512, "min_batch_time_ms":8}, "slot_compactor":{"enabled":true, "threshold":0.25}, "prefix_prefetch":true}
```

maya: applying to 3 canary nodes now.

deploy-bot: deploy started by maya on cluster eng-dedicated-canary (3/3 nodes). rollout id r-20260318-01.

riju: after patch applied, early telemetry looks better — no OOM hits on those nodes for the last 10 minutes, average mem headroom increased ~600MB. :thumbsup:

oliver: once stable, schedule an int4 calibration sweep — try layerwise per-channel scaling + small activation clipping. also run RNG-seed stability checks to rule out eval noise.

sasha: will re-run evals after 1 hour of stable traffic and post diffs. FYI baseline fp16->int4 used standard calibration dataset; maybe add domain-specific examples from summarization to calibration set.

alejandro: experiment matrix proposal (small):
- baseline int4 (current)
- int4 + domain-calib
- int4 + per-channel scale
- int4 + small-clip(6.0)
Measure ROUGE + p95 latency + mem peak. keep batch_size=4 for comparability.

maya: sounds good. I also want to try slightly increasing batch_size to 6 once mem stable to see throughput improvements; will watch p99 latency.

riju: one more note — logs showed kv_evicted=0 on evict attempts. we should lower kv_reserve for canary to avoid large prefetch windows stealing slots. set kv_reserve_pct from 20 -> 10 for canary.

alejandro: good call. add that to the config patch before widening rollout.

maya: updated patch applied (kv_reserve_pct=10). monitoring.

deploy-bot: rollout r-20260318-01 updated (kv_reserve_pct change).

maya: monitoring dashboard: after both changes (max_new_tokens=512 + kv_reserve_pct=10 + compactor) — 6% drop in OOM alerts for the canary, tail latency stable. will let it run for 2 hours then run the quality sweep.

sasha: posted eval diffs after 2h: int4 baseline -> int4 (domain-calib) -> int4 (per-channel) show ROUGE-1: 0.0, +1.1, +1.6 relative to int4 baseline. per-channel looks promising.

oliver: excellent. plan: keep canary config with max_new_tokens=512 and kv_reserve_pct=10 for next 24h, run full calibration sweep overnight, then consider bumping max_new_tokens back to 768 if mem/slo stable.

maya: thanks all. will file a small runbook for summit13b canary with the mitigations and fallback routing rule. cc: @sre for vis.

alejandro: please tag me on the runbook so I can add the experiment matrix. :eyes:
